cultural.vision_reason: This is a Japanese-made enamelware footed dish with lid, decorated with Ethiopian flags and photographic portraits of the Imperial family — a used/owned item of Ethiopian (Amhara-associated imperial) material culture, not a painting or manuscript. It is a metal vessel, so the claimed category is wrong but the ethnicity attribution is plausible.

physical.title: dish; lid
physical.summary:
Enamel footed dish with lid, Igaram sahan ; dish (a) has a white interior with predominantly royal blue stencilled decorations on the outer surface and representations of four Ethiopian flags. The base of the foot is inscribed with a makers mark of an anchor within a circle and the wording 'Anchor Made in Japan' and '20 c/m', which refers to the size.
lid (b) has a white interior and is decorated on the upper surface with blue stencilled designs with a central white cruciform motif. Each arm of the cross has a transfer photographic portrait of the Imperial family; (clockwise from bottom) Emperor Haile Selassie I of Ethiopia, shown with full beard, Empress Menen, Prince Makonnen, Duke of Harer and Crown Prince Asfaw Wossen. In the centre is a rounded handle with bands of red, yellow and green around the base.
